+  registered with a `slice` or `squeeze` parameter, and of a request with a
+  negative step. It keeps the registered selection apart from the array and
+  composes it with each requested slice, so Dask fuses a single slice into
+  the h5py read; a negative step is read forwards and reversed in memory.
+  Before, a corner of a registered row read the whole row, and a negative

+  A read of a single element keeps the dtype of the dataset; before,

design_notes: HDF5ArrayAdapter keeps the whole lazy Dask array of the files plus `_stencil`: the registered slice and squeeze as one expanded NDSlice of the files (squeeze = integer index of each selected length-1 dim, via a new `squeeze=` option of NDSlice.expand_for_shape). from_uris derives the structure from array[stencil] as before.

read(slice): expand the request for the structure shape, compose stencil[request] (compose_slices), and slice the base array once; read_block(block, slice): stencil[block_slice[inner]]. Dask fuses that single forward slice into each chunk's getter, so h5py reads exactly the requested elements.

Negative steps: Dask never fuses them (normalize_slice raises NotImplementedError, so whole chunks are read, even on PR #2 with no registered slice). The adapter turns the composed selection into a forward key plus a flip with PR #2's _forward_selection, computes, and flips in numpy; h5py never sees a negative step.

compose_slices was wrong for reversed slices that run to the start of an axis: a composed stop of -1 counts from the end (arr[0:10][::-1] -> slice(9,-1,-1), empty), and an expanded reversed left slice (stop negative) was refused by is_expanded and its length miscomputed. Fixed via a shared _slice_range helper (also used by _num_steps): compose through range slicing, negative stop -> None, empty -> slice(0,0); is_expanded accepts reversed slices with negative/None stop. The hypothesis strategy never drew such slices (its emptiness filter was wrong) and now does; it fails on PR #2.

Fallback: when the catalog structure shape differs from the registered array's (file grown past it, reshape, DataNotReady/IncompatibleShape), _read goes through force_reshape on the registered view as before; that path is NOT byte-exact (unchanged from PR #2).

Scalar/empty/vlen/multi-file: same values, shapes, chunks as PR #2. Every read now returns numpy.asarray(result, dtype=dataset dtype) on both paths (fast and force_reshape fallback), so a 0-d read is a 0-d ndarray with the dataset's byte order and string width; no copy when the dtype already matches (same object, or a view for h5py's big-endian dtype instance).

NDSlice.expand_for_shape gives a reversed slice that runs to the start of an axis stop=None (ndindex gives -n-1). is_expanded takes a reversed slice only with start >= 0 and stop None or >= 0, so an unexpanded relative negative stop is refused again (ValueError, as PR #2). split_1d and split_slice's preferred-split filter accept a None stop as well as ndindex's negative one; _slice_range/_num_steps keep tolerating negative stops. Client requests for such slices now go out as e.g. '9::-1' instead of '9:-11:-1' (same elements).
